newsitem.title: UK: AIC says Cargill fails to lift IPE November gas oil.
newsitem.headline: AIC says Cargill fails to lift IPE November gas oil.

text.p: Trading house Cargill has failed to lift the required volume of gas oil during the first five-day period of the November IPE contract, said a spokesman for AIC, the supplier of the oil.
They failed to lift about 40 percent of the volume from Antwerp and a further 15 to 20 percent of the volume from Amsterdam, he said.
Cargill was due to take delivery of 627,800 tonnes, of which a third each is due to be lifted in the three five-day periods, November 16-20, November 21-25 and November 26-30.
"It's clearly a default," said the spokesman. "They didn't present the vessels on time" at the loading installations. The deadline for loading in the first five-day period was midnight on Wednesday.
"If they try squeeze the market they have a responsibility to perform and lift the oil," he added.

International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) chief executive Lynton Jones said on Wednesday the exchange was closely monitoring the delivery of the November gas oil futures contract to ensure performance by the dominant short and long.
"We are closely monitoring what is going on and are in contact with the parties," Jones said by telephone.
"We monitor each of these (five-day) periods to make sure performance has taken place. In case of any allegation that performance has not taken place, we clearly have an interest.
"So if there is a technical default, either party can refer the matter to arbitration. The (IPE) directors then have to determine the price at which the products will be invoiced back."
Jones added that in some cases the price could include a premium to reflect compensation for the aggrieved party.

European gas oil traders have condemned a duel being fought between two big trading houses on gas oil futures, saying it has killed liquidity, distorted supply patterns and blunted the IPE's price discovery function.

Some infuriated traders called on the IPE to impose stiffer penalties on attempted squeezes. They warned that the IPE's status as the ultimate source of physical gas oil was at stake in what one player called a "battle of the giants" between two of Europe's main gas oil traders.

"Conditions are chaotic. It's ridiculous. There are huge supply hiccups. There are no barges available to move product into Germany and it's impossible to run a sensible hedge," one trader said. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4948
